baseline.note:
Subjective: 55-year-old male with type 2 diabetes presents for routine review. Reports increased thirst for 1 month and nocturia (2 times nightly). occasional toe numbness, likely cold‑induced. No visual changes; last eye exam in March was normal. Diet: increased sweets since retirement. Medication adherence: Metformin 500 mg BID, missing evening dose 2‑3 times/week. No hypoglycemia. No smoking; occasional weekend wine.
Objective: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 92 kg (up from 89 kg in June). Foot exam: palpable pulses, intact skin, no ulcers; reduced monofilament sensation on left big toe. HbA1c 64 mmol/mol.
Assessment: Suboptimal glycemic control with symptomatic polyuria/polydipsia, weight gain, and early peripheral neuropathy. Risk of diabetic foot complications (family history of toe amputation).
Plan: 1) Increase Metformin dose (e.g., to 500 mg TID or consider extended‑release formulation). 2) Reinforce adherence, especially evening dose. 3) Refer to diabetic foot clinic for neuropathy monitoring. 4) Counsel on diet modification to reduce sweets and support weight loss. 5) Continue current lifestyle (no smoking, limit alcohol). 6) Repeat HbA1c in 3 months; monitor blood pressure.
